blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Estimating semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. While the recent progress in foundation models has significantly advanced solutions for such difficult image correspondence problems, respective methods are often insufficiently regularised. For example, common nearest-neighbour matching with foundation model features often results in noisy correspondences, which is particularly prominent when solving for dense correspondences. In this work, we tackle image matching via functional maps, which have been popularised for 3D shape matching due to their powerful spectral formalism utilising an efficient low-dimensional linear representation. However, functional maps require that domains (in our cases the rectangular image grids) are equipped with an informative and non-trivial geometry. To define a meaningful manifold structure for images, we use Galerkin's method from finite elements to derive a discrete Laplace-Beltrami operator (LBO) based on a manifold embedding of deep image features. Further, we leverage a neural adjoint map that allows to represent non-linear mappings. We demonstrate that our method sets the new state of the art among zero-shot image correspondence methods on multiple dense correspondence benchmarks of real-world images. Our code is publicly available: https://github.com/NafieAmrani/NAMI
blocks.zh: 估计现实世界图像中类似类别的不同对象实例之间的语义对应是计算机视觉中的一个根本挑战. 虽然最近在基础模型方面取得的进展大大推动了解决这些难以解决的图像对应问题,但各种方法往往不够规范。 例如,常见的近邻与基础模型特征的匹配往往导致杂音通信,在解决稠密通信时尤为突出. 在这部作品中,我们通过功能地图处理图像匹配问题,由于这些图具有强大的光谱形式,利用高效的低维线性表现,因此3D形状匹配已被普及. 然而,功能图要求域(就我们的情况而言,是长方形图像网格)配备信息丰富且非三角几何. 为了定义图像的有意义的多重结构,我们用Galerkin的方法从有限的元素中得出一个离散的Laplace-Beltrami操作符(LBO),基于深层图像特征的多重嵌入. 此外,我们利用一个能代表非线性绘图的神经连接图。 我们证明,我们的方法将新艺术定位在零镜头图像对应方法中,在现实世界图像的多重密集对应基准上. 我们的代码可公开查阅:https://github.com/NafieAmrani/NAMI

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Finding (semantic) correspondences across images is a fundamental task in computer vision, as it forms a prerequisite for numerous downstream tasks, such as image registration and stitching [ 1 ] , 3D reconstruction [ 2 , 3 ] , structure-from-motion [ 4 ] ,
and many more. Recent foundation models, such as DINO [ 5 , 6 ] or CLIP [ 7 ] have been demonstrated to lead to powerful feature descriptors that are well-suited to establish image correspondences [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] .
Most commonly, respective feature descriptors are matched based on a simple nearest-neighbour (NN) routine [ 8 ] .
NN matching is generally reliable for finding sparse correspondences. However, it lacks a sense of global structure, such as semantic or geometric context, which often results in unreliable and unsmooth results. These issues are particularly evident when using NN to establish dense image matchings.
blocks.zh:
查找图像之间的(语义)对应是计算机视觉中的一项基本任务,因为它是众多下游任务的前提,例如图像注册和缝合[1],3D重建[2,3],结构-从动. [4],
还有更多 最近的基础模型,如DINO [5,6] 或CLIP [7] 已被证明导致强大的特征描述,这些描述非常适合建立图像对应[8,9,10].
最常见的是,根据一个简单的近邻(NN)常规[8]来匹配相应的特征描述符.
NN匹配一般对寻找稀疏的函文是可靠的. 然而,它缺乏一种全球结构感,如语义或几何背景,往往导致不可靠和不平稳的结果. 在利用NN建立密集图像匹配时,这些问题尤其明显.

blocks.en:
Dense matching problems are also omnipresent in 3D shape analysis; among the most successful approaches for 3D shape matching are deep functional map methods [ 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 ] that build upon the functional maps (FM) framework [ 15 ] .
Instead of matching points directly, functional maps operate on low-dimensional function spaces represented by low-rank matrices. In the context of 3D geometry, these spaces are typically spanned by the spectral basis of the LBO ; this low-dimensional representation effectively regularises the matching, allowing the problem to be solved in a coordinate system defined by the shape’s own intrinsic geometry.
After optimisation, dense shape correspondences can be recovered from the low-rank matrix.
Overall, the utility and success of the FM framework originates in the use of informative and explicit geometric information of the 3D shapes. Despite its success for 3D shape matching, so far the FM framework is underexplored for finding correspondences across 2D images – this is because of the severe challenge that images do not explicitly give rise to informative geometric information.
blocks.zh:
3D形状分析中也无处不出现强烈的匹配问题;3D形状匹配最成功的方法包括基于功能地图(FM)框架的深功能地图方法[11,12,13,14].
功能地图不是直接匹配点,而是在低阶矩阵所代表的低维函数空间上运行. 在3D几何学中,这些空间通常被LBO的光谱基础所跨越;这种低维的表示法有效地规范了匹配,使得问题能够在由形状本身的内在几何学定义的坐标系统中得到解决.
优化后,密集的形状对应可以从低阶矩阵中恢复.
总体而言,调频框架的效用和成功源于使用3D形状的丰富和明确的几何信息. 尽管在3D形状匹配上取得了成功,但到目前为止,FM框架对于在2D图像中寻找对应信息探索不足——这是因为图像没有明确产生信息化几何信息的严重挑战.

blocks.en:
In this work, we explore how to best exploit the FM framework for finding correspondences across 2D images .
Although (natural) images represent 2D projections of geometric (and textured) 3D objects, the resulting images are (geometrically) flat. Thus, they do not allow direct access to the underlying geometric information. Recent work proposed to represent an image in terms of a 4-connected pixel graph, where an exponential kernel applied to distances of deep features is used to obtain edge weights [ 16 ] . However, major drawbacks of this approach are the ad-hoc choice of a scale parameter and the resulting weak theoretical properties.
blocks.zh:
我们探索如何最佳利用调频框架,
虽然(自然)图像代表了几何(和纹理)3D物体的2D投影,但由此产生的图像是(几何)平的. 因此,它们不允许直接获取基本的几何信息。 最近的工作建议用4个连成一体的像素图来代表一个图像,其中一个适用于深层特征距离的指数内核用来获得边缘重量[16]. 然而,这种办法的主要缺点是临时选择一个尺度参数以及由此产生的薄弱的理论属性。

blocks.en:
Our approach circumvents this by introducing a geometric manifold embedding of deep image features. From a technical point of view, we interpret each feature as a high-dimensional vertex coordinate for a quad mesh given by the image grid, so that we can apply Galerkin’s method from finite elements to derive a discrete LBO .
This avoids choosing a scale parameter and inherits theoretical properties from variational methods [ 17 ] .
Further, we have found that within our manifold embedding framework, the standard functional map approach (a linear transform on truncated spectral bases) loses too much information to be sufficiently expressive (see Fig. 5 ). Hence, we leverage the recently introduced Neural Adjoint Map (NAM) [ 14 ] approach, which compensates for this truncation-induced loss by aligning our manifold embeddings non-linearly within the truncated subspace. Overall, we demonstrate that our novel framework obtains compelling experimental results across a range of different settings (see Fig. 1 ).
We summarise our contributions as follows: 1. For the first time, we introduce a manifold embedding of deep image features, which we combine with NAMs to address the image correspondence problem. 2. Unlike the previous functional map-based image matching method [ 16 ] , our manifold embedding perspective leads to a discrete LBO that does not require choosing a scale parameter and inherits favourable theoretical properties from variational methods. 3. Experimentally, we show that we outperform existing zero-shot baselines in dense real-world image correspondence benchmarks. Further, we illustrate the advantage of our zero-shot approach by applying it to other domains such as medical image matching.
blocks.zh:
我们的方法通过引入深层图像特征的几何多重嵌入来规避这一点。 从技术角度看,我们把每个特性解释为图像网格给出的四元网格的高维顶点坐标,这样我们就可以从有限的元素中应用Gallerkin的方法来得出离散的LBO.
这避免了选择一个比例参数,并从变异方法继承理论属性[17].
此外,我们发现,在我们多重嵌入框架内,标准功能图方法(短光谱基上的线性转换)损失的信息过多,无法充分表达(见图5)。 因此,我们利用最近推出的神经辅助地图[14]方法,通过将我们的多层嵌入非线性地放在短小空间中来补偿这种短小引起的损失。 总的来说,我们表明,我们的新框架在一系列不同的场合取得了令人信服的实验结果(见图1)。
我们的贡献总结如下: 1. 我们首次引入了深层图像特征的多重嵌入,我们与不结盟运动联合处理图像对应问题。 2. 与之前的基于功能映射的图像匹配方法[16]不同,我们的多嵌入视角导致一个离散的LBO,不需要选择比例参数,并从变异方法继承有利的理论属性. 3. 在实验中,我们显示,在密集的现实世界图像对应基准中,我们的表现超过了现有的零射基线。 此外,我们通过将零射法应用于医学图像匹配等其他领域来说明我们零射法的优点。

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
The functional map framework, first introduced by Ovsjanikov et al. [15] , has become a well-established paradigm for non-rigid 3D shape matching.
Rather than solving for pointwise correspondences through an expensive combinatorial optimisation problem [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 ] , functional maps operate in the functional domain.
To this end, correspondence relationships are encoded into a compact matrix, known as the functional map, which represents a linear transformation between spectral embeddings.
Due to its inherent simplicity and efficiency, the framework has been extended to improve robustness [ 23 , 24 ] , facilitate multishape matching [ 25 ] , and address non-isometric [ 26 , 27 ] or partial shape matching [ 28 ] .
However, severe partiality remains a known challenge for functional maps as core underlying assumptions degrade [ 29 ] , motivating alternative shape-matching frameworks [ 30 ] .
Furthermore, shifting from traditional methods dependent on hand-crafted features [ 31 , 32 ] , functional maps have been integrated into both supervised [ 11 , 33 ] and unsupervised [ 12 , 13 ] deep learning architectures, enabling applications ranging from medical 3D image matching [ 34 , 35 , 36 ] to latent representation alignment [ 37 ] .
While the standard functional map framework parametrises the alignment between truncated spectral bases as a linear transformation, recent work has introduced a non-linear formalism [ 14 ] . This extension recovers expressivity lost to spectral truncation, information that no linear operator on the truncated coefficients can represent, and has yielded superior results in 3D shape matching.
blocks.zh:
功能地图框架,最早由Ovsjanikov等人提出. [15],已经成为非刚性3D形状匹配的既定范式.
功能图不是通过昂贵的组合优化问题[18,19,20,21,22]来解决指针通信,而是在功能域中运行.
为此,通信关系被编码成一个紧凑的矩阵,称为功能图,代表光谱嵌入之间的线性转变.
由于其内在的简单和高效,该框架被扩展,以提高稳健性[23,24],促进多形状匹配[25],并解决非同位素[26,27]或部分形状匹配[28].
然而,对于功能图来说,严重的偏差仍然是已知的挑战,因为核心基础假设退化[29],促使备选的形状匹配框架[30]。
此外,从依赖手工制作的特征的传统方法[31、32],功能图已经融入了受监督的[11、33]和无监督的[12、13]深层学习架构,使各种应用得以实现,从医学三维图像匹配[34、35、36]到潜在表达式匹配[37]。
虽然标准功能映射框架将截断光谱基之间的对齐化为线性转变,但近期的工作引入了非线性形式主义[14]. 这个扩展恢复了光谱切变失去的表达性,即切变系数上的线性操作者无法代表的信息,并在3D形状匹配上取得了优异的结果.

blocks.en:
Despite these advancements in 3D, applying functional maps to 2D images remains challenging.
Treating images as geometric surfaces rather than flat regular grids has a rich history, ranging from classical PDE and anisotropic scale-space formulations [ 38 , 39 , 40 , 41 , 42 ] to modern geometric operator theory [ 43 ] , yet a discretisation suited to functional maps is still lacking.
Early works [ 44 , 45 ] represented images as graphs via super-pixel decompositions, but the resulting eigenfunctions suffer from significant information loss.
To mitigate this, [ 16 ] recently built a graph from foundation model features. While improving performance, the resulting graph is an ad-hoc construction and without a geometric interpretation.
To address this, we propose using a discretised LBO of a 2D surface embedded in the high-dimensional feature space of foundational models.
blocks.zh:
尽管在3D中取得了这些进步,将功能地图应用到2D图像上仍然具有挑战性.
将图像作为几何表面而不是平整的正格,有着丰富的历史,从古典的PDE和异构的尺度-空间配体[38,39,40,41,42]到现代几何操作理论[43],然而仍然缺乏适合功能地图的光碟化.
早期的作品[44,45]通过超像素分解来代表图像作为图,但由此产生的eigen功能受到重大信息损失.
为了缓解这种情况,[16] 最近从基础模型特征中绘制了一个图表。 在改进性能的同时,由此产生的图是临时构造,没有几何解释.
为了解决这个问题,我们提议使用一个嵌入于基底模型高维特征空间的2D表面的盘状LBO.

blocks.en:
Semantic matching aims to establish keypoint correspondences by identifying functionally or contextually equivalent roles across images, regardless of appearance or pose variations. While we focus here on the developments most relevant to our approach, a more extensive review of the field is available in the recent survey by Zhang et al. [46] .
Traditional semantic correspondence frameworks extract features from images [ 47 , 48 , 49 ] , compute pairwise similarities through cost volume representations [ 50 , 51 , 52 ] and subsequently estimate the final matching field between images [ 53 , 54 , 55 ] .
As they rely on smooth displacement fields or locally varying affine transformations, these methods often fail to determine dense correspondences for complex articulated deformations.
To mitigate this, multiple works have introduced end-to-end regression techniques [ 56 , 57 , 50 ] or parameterized spatial priors [ 58 , 59 , 60 , 61 ] .
Other research directions have explored the prediction of semantic correspondences in weakly supervised settings via dense image alignment [ 62 , 63 ] ,
or through unsupervised frameworks via automatic label generation [ 64 , 65 , 66 ] .
blocks.zh:
语义匹配的目的是通过识别跨图像的功能或上下文等同的角色来建立关键点对应,而无论外观或构成变化. 虽然我们在此集中阐述与我们的方法最相关的事态发展,但张等人最近的调查对该领域作了更广泛的审查。 [46] (中文(简体) ).
传统的语义对应框架从图像中提取特征[47,48,49],通过成本量表示计算成对相似性[50,51,52],并随后估计图像之间的最终匹配场[53,54,55].
由于这些方法依赖于平滑的离散场或当地变化不定的亲缘变异,因此往往无法确定复杂清晰的变形的密函.
为缓解这种情况,多个作品引入了端对端回归技术[56,57,50]或参数化的空间前身[58,59,60,61].
其他研究方向探索了通过密集图像对齐[62,63],在受弱监督的环境下对语义函证的预测.
或通过无监督的框架通过自动标签生成[64,65,66].

blocks.en:
However, due to limited feature capacity or an over-reliance on strong spatial priors, these methods still struggle with challenging scenarios involving significant pose changes or pronounced changes in appearance between different instances of the same category, e.g . colour changes or non-rigid deformations.
To overcome this, we propose a non-linear, structure-aware formalism capable of enhancing matching fidelity without necessitating restrictive spatial priors.
blocks.zh:
然而,由于特征能力有限或过度依赖强力的空间前兆,这些方法仍然与具有挑战性的情景作斗争,这些情景涉及同一类别不同情况之间的显著变化或外观的明显变化,例如颜色变化或非刚性变形。
为了克服这种情况,我们建议一种非线性、有结构意识的形式主义,这种形式主义能够增强匹配的忠诚,而不必限制空间前科。

blocks.en:
While self-supervised and unsupervised learning methods have gained popularity [ 67 , 68 , 69 , 70 , 71 ] , those trained primarily on image-level objectives [ 71 , 68 , 72 ] often fail to capture fine-grained spatial details [ 73 , 74 ] .
To address this, recent advancements in patch-based methods [ 5 , 75 , 6 ] and diffusion models [ 76 , 77 , 78 , 79 ] have demonstrated increased robustness to geometric transformations, enabling the extraction of dense correspondences in zero-shot settings [ 9 , 10 , 74 ] .
Within the domain of image correspondence, Zhang et al. [8] established that combined features from DINOv2 [ 5 ] and Stable Diffusion [ 77 ] are sufficiently descriptive to achieve strong zero-shot performance using a simple nearest-neighbour search. Zhang et al. [80] further addressed left/right geometric ambiguities in such features.
blocks.zh:
虽然自我监督和不受监督的学习方法已经获得欢迎[67,68,69,70,71],但那些主要接受图像级目标培训的人[71,68,72]往往无法捕捉精细的空间细节[73,74].
为了解决这一问题,最近在补丁方法[5、75、6]和传播模型[76、77、78、79]方面的进步表明,几何转换的强性有所提高,从而能够在零发环境中提取密集的函文[9、10、74]。
在图像通信领域,张等. [8] 确定DINOv2[5]和稳定扩散[77]的组合特征足够描述性,可以使用简单的近邻搜索实现强烈的零镜头性能. 张等. [80] 进一步处理了这些特征的左/右几何模糊之处。

blocks.en:
Still, nearest neighbour search relies solely on the descriptiveness of the features and inherently lacks the contextual information provided by the image structure.
Building on existing spectral mapping methods [ 16 ] , we propose a framework that incorporates non-linear spectral mappings to regularise the matching and increase robustness towards ambiguous features and medical imagery.
blocks.zh:
然而,最近的邻居搜索完全依赖于特征的描述性,而且本质上缺乏图像结构提供的背景资料。
在现有光谱制图方法[16]的基础上,我们提议建立一个框架,纳入非线性光谱制图,使匹配正规化,并增强对模糊特征和医疗图像的稳健性。

blocks.en: 3 Background
blocks.zh: 3 背景情况

blocks.en:
The goal of our method is to establish correspondences between two images using the functional maps framework [ 15 ] . Depending on the point of view, we can represent such correspondences either continuously as a mapping T T between rectangular subsets of ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , or discretely as a permutation 𝚷 \boldsymbol{\Pi} of landmarks like pixels or features. The functional maps framework connects these two.
We will first discuss the functional maps framework for general manifolds in Section 3.1 . We will then apply it to image matching in Section 4 by equipping the flat image with a manifold structure.

blocks.en:
To facilitate robust feature matching from a source image ℐ s \mathcal{I}_{s} to a target image ℐ t \mathcal{I}_{t} , we propose the optimisation of a NAM [ 14 ] with an LBO specifically computed for images. Our framework assumes that for each feature patch on the source image there exists a semantic counterpart in the target image as in [ 16 ] .
The pipeline is presented in Fig. 2 and begins by extracting two sets of features 𝑬 s \boldsymbol{E}_{s} and 𝑭 s \boldsymbol{F}_{s} for the source image from two frozen, off-the-shelf foundation models (e.g. DINO [ 5 ] or Stable Diffusion [ 77 ] ). Next, the features 𝑬 s \boldsymbol{E}_{s} and 𝑬 t \boldsymbol{E}_{t} are used to construct an LBO for the input images to extract spectral embeddings.
Finally, the features 𝑭 s \boldsymbol{F}_{s} and 𝑭 t \boldsymbol{F}_{t} , alongside the spectral embeddings, are utilised to train our NAM . These stages are discussed in detail in the following sections.

blocks.en:
We model deep neural feature maps as uniform grid-samples drawn from an underlying continuous surface.
For regular spatial grids, bilinear basis functions provide a canonical choice for discretization.
By employing the Galerkin formulation [ 17 ] , Céa’s lemma [ 84 ] guarantees that our discrete LBO yields the optimal approximation of the continuous LBO within the span of this finite-dimensional basis.
This approximation bound directly yields transformation stability: potential equivariances of the input features such as rotations or translations in the image domain correspond to isometric reparametrisations of the continuous surface.
Consequently, while rigid transformations yield distinct discrete grid samples, and thus distinct discrete operator matrices, both discrete representations consistently approximate the same underlying continuous LBO , preserving equivariance across representations.

Céa的lemma[84]通过使用Gallerkin配方,保证我们的离散LBO在这一有限维基范围内产生连续LBO的最佳近似值。
这种近似绑定直接产生变换稳定性:图像域中旋转或翻译等输入特性的潜在等价值对应连续表面的同位素重整.
因此,虽然刚性变换产生不同的离散网格样本,从而产生不同的离散运营方矩阵,但这两种离散的表示始终大致相同,具有连续的LBO,保持了各种表示的均匀性。

We conduct an ablation study to evaluate the contribution of each component in our framework, for which we consider varying numbers of eigenfunctions, see Fig. 5 .
First, to validate our proposed image-based LBO , we replace it with the graph Laplacian used in [ 16 ] (plotted in blue).
Second, we assess the impact of the NAM by replacing it with a linear functional map based framework (SmoothFM) [ 97 ] (plotted in green).
For completeness, we additionally report the combination of both substitutions (plotted in purple).
Our method achieves superior performance across all configurations, with k = 50 k=50 representing the optimal setting for our approach.
While lower k k values reduce high-frequency detail, they provide critical regularisation for the ambiguous DINO + SD features. This regularisation is needed, as evidenced by our nearest-neighbour results.
Conversely, larger values of k k degrade performance, a behaviour inherited from functional map based methods, for which an optimal number of eigenfunctions is well known [ 23 ] . Appendix F confirms that both components exhibit identical behaviour on SPair-71k [ 89 ] .

blocks.en: 6 Discussion & limitations
blocks.zh: 6 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
Although our method produces overall high-quality correspondences, it also possesses some drawbacks:
(i) Our formulation assumes that every source point has a counterpart in the target image. For dense image matching this breaks down under heavy occlusion or large pose differences – yet, our sparse matching experiments cover such cases by matching the set of given keypoints, see Fig. A13 .
Extending our framework to dense partial-to-partial matching, e.g. by predicting overlapping regions as done for 3D partial shapes in [ 33 , 98 ] , is a promising direction for future work.
(ii) Further, our framework constructs semantic mappings by introducing an image-specific LBO derived from vision foundation model features.
Because these features encapsulate a blend of semantic, geometric, and appearance information, the resulting operator represents a combination of these attributes, rather than an explicit description of 3D geometry.
With that, our LBO equips the feature space with an abstract geometric notion that facilitates spatial alignment.
(iii) In addition, functional maps use intrinsic properties of the manifolds to be matched. As such, the matching may flip if the deep feature embedding exhibits symmetries. Such a semantic symmetry may occur for near-symmetric images, e.g . the trains in Fig. 3 . This example also confirms that it is task-dependent whether such a flip is desirable or not.
(iv) Furthermore, the precision of our mappings is currently constrained by the resolution of the underlying image features, particularly when employing patch-based backbones such as DINO.
However, our formalism is compatible with higher-resolution representations and can naturally be extended to upsampled [ 99 ] or pixel-level feature extractors once they become available.
blocks.zh:
虽然我们的方法产生了总体的高质量函证,但也有一些缺点:
(i) 我们的表述假设,每个源点在目标图像中都有对应点。 对于在重隐蔽或大块的布局下破损的密集图像来说 — — 然而,我们稀少的配对实验通过匹配给定的密钥来覆盖这些病例,请参见Fig. A13。
将我们的框架扩大到密集的局部与局部的匹配,例如通过预测[33,98]中3D部分形状的重叠区域,是未来工作的一个有希望的方向。
(二) 此外,我们的框架通过引入基于视觉基础模型特征的图像专用LBO来构建语义制图。
因为这些特征囊括了语义,几何,和外观信息的混合,因此产生的操作员代表了这些属性的组合,而不是对3D几何的明确描述.
由此,我们的LBO为特色空间配备了一个抽象的几何概念,方便空间对齐.
(三) 此外,功能图还使用要匹配的多元体的内在属性. 因此,如果深层特性嵌入了物证对称性,匹配可能会翻转. 这种语义对称可能发生在近对称图像上,例如图3中的列车. 这个例子还证实,这种翻转是否可取取决于任务。
(四) 此外,我们制图的精确度目前受到基本图像特征解析的制约,特别是在使用诸如DINO等基于补丁的骨干时。
然而,我们的形式主义与更高分辨率的表示相容,在得到像素级特征提取器后,自然可以扩展为被检测的[99]或像素级特征提取器.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We have presented a novel framework for finding semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images. To achieve this, we consider a spectral matching formalism building upon the functional maps framework, which so far has been mainly popularised in the domain of 3D shape matching. Unlike previous spectral image matching methods, our approach leverages a well-principled LBO for 2D images that is derived via a manifold embedding of deep image features. With that, we show that the recent advances in foundation models allow us to equip the otherwise flat image with a meaningful manifold structure.
Overall, our work demonstrates that well-established geometric principles can be transferred and utilised to successfully tackle fundamental challenges in image-based correspondence problems, thereby bridging the fields of 3D geometry processing and 2D computer vision.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了一个新颖的框架,在现实世界的图像中寻找不同类别对象之间的语义对应。 为了实现这一目标,我们考虑在功能地图框架的基础上建立一个光谱匹配形式主义,到目前为止,它主要在3D形状匹配领域被普及. 与之前的光谱图像匹配方法不同,我们的方法利用了通过深层图像特征的多重嵌入而得到的2D图像的原理良好的LBO. 因此,我们表明,最近基础模型的进展使我们能够为本来平坦的图像配备有意义的多重结构。
总之,我们的工作表明,可以转让和利用既定的几何原则,成功地解决基于图像的函证问题的根本挑战,从而弥合三维几何处理和二维计算机视觉领域。

blocks.en: Appendix B Implementation details
blocks.zh: 附录B

blocks.en:
We present the implementation details of our method. The optimisation is implemented in PyTorch and uses the Adam optimiser with a learning rate of 10 − 2 10^{-2} for training the NAM model.
Training is performed for 200 iterations. NAM consists of a linear branch (a bias-free fully connected layer, equivalent to a standard functional map) and a non-linear residual branch (an MLP with two hidden layers of width 128 128 and LeakyReLU activations). The MLP output is scaled by 0.01 0.01 and added to the linear branch, so h θ h_{\theta} behaves as a linear map at initialisation and learns non-linear corrections during training. Weights are initialised with Xavier uniform. See [ 14 ] for more details.

blocks.en: Appendix D Spectral refinement

blocks.en:
Our method optionally admits a spectral refinement step via Neural ZoomOut (NZO) [ 14 ] .
NZO progressively grows the spectral embedding by alternating between two conversions: from a point-to-point map to an NAM at the current dimension, and from the NAM back to a point-to-point map via nearest-neighbour search. In our experiments, we grow the embedding size from 50 50 to 250 250 in increments of 40 40 . Table A4 compares our method with and without NZO. Throughout the rest of the paper, we report results without NZO in order to characterise the performance of our method on its own.

blocks.en: H.1 Synthetic dataset creation

blocks.en: We construct a new dataset, which we refer to as Faust-2D , by building on FAUST [ 101 ] , a well-established benchmark for 3D shape matching that provides vertex-wise correspondences between all of its shapes. Our pipeline proceeds as follows: 1. We render pairs of FAUST shapes (registered scans of different people in different poses) as source and target images. 2. Each image pair is passed to SDXL [ 102 ] to generate a plausible background from one of 14 categories (e.g. office, living room, kitchen, cafe, gym, library, retail store). 3. The foreground is passed through a ControlNet inpainting model [ 103 ] to texturise the FAUST shapes. 4. We blend the texturised foreground and the generated background into a single image. This yields 380 image pairs of texturised FAUST shapes with automatically generated backgrounds; Fig. A8 shows representative examples. For each pair, we compute pixel-to-pixel ground-truth correspondences via a visibility test from the given camera angle. Shapes are randomly rotated by angles between 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} and 140 ∘ 140^{\circ} , which lets us stratify the pairs by the relative rotation between the two shapes into easy ( 0 ∘ 0^{\circ} – 20 ∘ 20^{\circ} ), medium ( 20 ∘ 20^{\circ} – 80 ∘ 80^{\circ} ), and hard ( 80 ∘ 80^{\circ} – 140 ∘ 140^{\circ} ) cases.

blocks.en: We conduct an ablation study to assess the contribution of each component of our framework, evaluating every variant across a range of eigenfunction counts K K ( Fig. A9 ). Our LBO outperforms the graph Laplacian, and the NAM outperforms SmoothFM [ 97 ] . The plots also show that the best-performing value is K = 100 K=100 on Faust-2D , whereas on TSS we found K = 50 K=50 to be optimal. This is consistent with the known sensitivity of functional-map methods to K K : performance peaks at an intermediate value and declines on either side, with the location of that peak depending on the dataset.

blocks.en: Appendix J Robustness to initialisation
blocks.zh: 附录J 初始化的能力

blocks.en: Since our method involves an instance-specific optimisation of the NAM , the final correspondence depends on the random initialisation of the network weights. To assess the robustness of our method to this choice, we run our pipeline with ten different random seeds on the TSS dataset and report the mean and standard deviation across all metrics in Table A9 . The low standard deviations across all metrics indicate that our method is robust to the choice of initialisation, and that the reported performance is not the result of a particularly favourable seed.

blocks.en:
Although the combination of SD (v3.5) and DINOv2-ViT-L/14 achieves the best performance, we select SD (v1.5) with DINOv2-ViT-B/14 as the default configuration for our method.
This choice provides a favourable trade-off between performance and model size, ViT-B/14 (86M parameters) compared with ViT-L/14 (300M parameters), while also enabling direct comparison with existing baselines that employ SD (v1.5).
Interestingly, using the same backbone for both LBO extraction and NAM training performs worse than combining different networks. This suggests that different backbones, specifically SD and DINOv2, provide complementary representations, which is consistent with the observations of Zhang et al. [8] .
Furthermore, combinations of SD with DINOv2 variants consistently outperform those using SD with DINOv3 variants.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Our first contribution outlines the overarching framework implemented in this paper. The second is detailed within the methodology section, while the third is demonstrated through both the experimental results and the appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We discuss in details the limitations of our work in the limitation section and provide potential future research directions. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No theoretical results are presented in the paper. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All details required to reproduce our results using the publicly available datasets are discussed in Appendix B . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The datasets used in this work are publicly available and the code is published (see link in abstract). Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We discuss how we use the datasets in the experimental setup section, we also add the hyperparameters and type of optimiser in the implementation details in Appendix B . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We run an analysis of the robustness of our method to initialisation of the weights of the NAM and report the results in Appendix J . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We report our runtime in the result section for our main experiment and we provide the compute resources used in Appendix B . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We have reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and believe that our work conforms to this code. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [N/A] Justification: Semantic correspondence is a fundamental computer-vision problem without direct societal impact. However, our method could affect downstream applications such as autonomous driving and medical image analysis, where improved accuracy may contribute positively to safety and diagnostics, but errors could also propagate negatively in safety-critical contexts. We encourage practitioners to validate the method within their specific deployment setting. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No such risks are foreseen by our work. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All publicly available datasets used in this work have been correctly cited. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是]理由: 我们的第一次发言概述了本文件实施的总体框架。 第二点在方法部分详细列出,第三点通过实验结果和附录加以证明。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在限制部分详细讨论了我们工作的局限性,并提供了今后可能的研究方向。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 文件没有提出理论结果。 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 附录B讨论了使用公开数据集复制我们的结果所需的所有细节。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 本作品中使用的数据集是公开的,并发布代码(见抽象链接). · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们讨论了如何使用实验设置部分的数据集,我们还在附录B的执行细节中增加了超参数和选择型号。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们分析了我们启动不结盟运动权重的方法是否有力,并在附录J中报告了结果。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们报告我们的主要试验结果部分的运行时间,并提供附录B所用的计算资源。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 我们审查了《新IPS道德守则》,认为我们的工作符合该守则。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答:[N/A] 理由:语义通信是一个基本的计算机-视觉问题,没有直接的社会影响. 然而,我们的方法可能会影响下游的应用,如自主驾驶和医疗图像分析,在这些应用中,精确度的提高可能有利于安全和诊断,但在安全关键背景下,错误也可能消极传播。 我们鼓励从业人员在其具体的部署范围内验证这一方法。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 我们的工作没有预见到这种风险。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 在这项工作中使用的所有公开数据集均已正确引用。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 在这项工作范围内没有释放新的资产。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 在编写本文件时,没有针对人类主题进行任何多方参与或研究。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 在编写本文件时,没有针对人类主题进行任何多方参与或研究。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[不详]理由: 没有使用LLMS开发这一研究的核心方法. · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Our first contribution outlines the overarching framework implemented in this paper. The second is detailed within the methodology section, while the third is demonstrated through both the experimental results and the appendix.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们的第一次发言概述了本文件实施的总体框架。 第二点在方法部分详细列出,第三点通过实验结果和附录加以证明。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]

blocks.en: Justification: We discuss in details the limitations of our work in the limitation section and provide potential future research directions.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

blocks.en: Theory assumptions and proofs
blocks.zh: 理论假设和证明

blocks.en: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
blocks.zh: 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No theoretical results are presented in the paper.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件没有提出理论结果。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.

blocks.en: Experimental result reproducibility
blocks.zh: 实验结果可复制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: All details required to reproduce our results using the publicly available datasets are discussed in Appendix B .
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 附录B讨论了使用公开数据集复制我们的结果所需的所有细节。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Justification: Semantic correspondence is a fundamental computer-vision problem without direct societal impact. However, our method could affect downstream applications such as autonomous driving and medical image analysis, where improved accuracy may contribute positively to safety and diagnostics, but errors could also propagate negatively in safety-critical contexts. We encourage practitioners to validate the method within their specific deployment setting.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.zh: 现有资产的许可证

blocks.en: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: All publicly available datasets used in this work have been correctly cited.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 在这项工作中使用的所有公开数据集均已正确引用。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No new assets are released within the scope of this work.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 在这项工作范围内没有释放新的资产。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects have been conducted in the preparation of this paper.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 在编写本文件时,没有针对人类主题进行任何多方参与或研究。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects have been conducted in the preparation of this paper.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 在编写本文件时,没有针对人类主题进行任何多方参与或研究。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
